column1: # Where each woven Italian verb form in lex-it.tsv was read.
# A verb row weaves its second form under an English -ing, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. Italian weaves the gerund,
# the gerundio of "sto dicendo". Its present participle is another word,
# dicente, which the seed's header named for every language until
# 2026-10-08 and which the pack does not weave. That day every woven
# Italian form was read in the "gerund" row of the conjugation table on
# English Wiktionary's Italian entry for its verb, rendered as a reader
# sees it, because a verb's headword line prints none of its gerunds. All
# 80 are the form a table prints, and none was changed.
# quote is the row's label and its cell, as printed. The table marks the
# stressed vowel of every form, "dicèndo", where the spelling writes an
# accent only on a final vowel, so the test sets a mark on any other vowel
# aside. One infinitive is pronominal: sedersi's own table prints its gerund
# with the pronoun joined, "sedèndosi", and the pack weaves the gerund
# without it, sedendo, because si may stand before the verb that carries
# it, "si sta sedendo", so its line cites sedersi's entry and sedere's,
# Whether that form answers to every English -ing it is woven under — the
# progressive's participle, or a gerund used as a noun, "reading is fun" —
# is a call about the language rather than a lookup, written up in TODO.md
